business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Turbine-Driven Critical Care Invasive Ventilators

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Marshall Islands (Unitary National Corporate Registry, Majuro)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: U.S.-modeled statutory common law (Associations Law / Business Corporations Act) with residual Micronesian customary-law elements; no sub-state registry tier; corporate registry administration is centralized in Majuro.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Amended Compact of Free Association between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (2003), including trade, investment, and economic assistance provisions
Protocol on the Accession of the Republic of the Marshall Islands to the World Trade Organization (effective 2020)
Bilateral United States–Marshall Islands taxation arrangements covering international shipping and aircraft income, administered in coordination with the maritime registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act (Associations Law, Chapter 2), as amended, including Parts governing registered agents; Beneficial Ownership Act 2021, as amended, together with the Registrar of Corporations' Beneficial Ownership (Transparency) Regulations; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018, as amended, administered by the Financial Intelligence Office (FIO) of the Ministry of Finance; domestic transposition of FATF Recommendations 10, 24, and 25.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — beneficial ownership records are maintained exclusively by licensed RMI registered agents and mirrored into the Registrar of Corporations' internal electronic UBO Register; access is limited to the Registrar, the FIO, and designated prosecutorial authorities acting under lawful demand; there is no public UBO register and no public inspection right for non-resident business corporations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent corporate status certificate for each legal-person shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation (e.g., Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — the Republic of the Marshall Islands is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; the certificate must be notarized where the shareholder is incorporated, endorsed by the competent state-level authenticating authority, authenticated by the U.S. Department of State Authentication Office (for U.S.-issued documents), and legalized by the RMI Embassy in Washington, D.C. or another RMI consular post; alternatively, the chain runs through the RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Majuro, for inward-legalized instruments

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney and Registered Agent Engagement Agreement in favor of the licensed RMI registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of signature and the licensed RMI registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization chain: notarial certification, competent state-level authentication in the home jurisdiction, RMI consular legalization, and deposition of the original with the licensed registered agent as repository of the UBO and corporate records

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports, residential address proofs, and bank source-of-funds letters for all directors, shareholders, and individuals holding 25% or more ultimate beneficial ownership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport authorities, notaries public, and licensed banks in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or, in the alternative, certified-copy attestation executed by the licensed RMI registered agent applying FIO-prescribed KYC standards; OFAC, UN, EU, and domestic FIO screening must be re-run before the 90th day after attestation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, beneficial owners at or above the 25% threshold, the registered agent, and signatories against: (i) OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists; (iii) European Union financial sanctions lists; (iv) the RMI FIO domestic designation list; and (v) adverse-media and negative-news databases. Foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates require written senior-management approval under enhanced due diligence (EDD), a documented source-of-wealth narrative, and a risk rating maintained in the UBO file. Screening must be refreshed within 30 days before the initial filing of the Articles of Incorporation and every 90 days thereafter. Any positive match triggers a Suspicious Transaction Report to the FIO within 24 hours and an immediate freeze on the incorporation process pending lawful clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro — Corporate Registry Information System (CRIS); name searches and reservations are submitted exclusively through licensed RMI registered agents; no anonymous direct-public web portal exists for foreign applicants.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory filings are in English; a corporate name must employ Latin-script characters; Arabic numerals, ampersands, commas, periods, and standard permitted abbreviations are acceptable in registry practice; names derived from non-Latin scripts must be accompanied by a notarized official English transliteration, and that transliteration must be phonetically distinguishable from every name already appearing in the register; there is no Marshallese-script or local-language naming mandate for non-resident business corporations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant, acting through its licensed registered agent, may file a Request for Reconsideration with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 calendar days, attaching any ministerial approval or letters of consent relevant to the sensitive token, amended distinguishing name variants, and the statutory reconsideration fee. The Registrar must issue a written determination within 14 business days. A further administrative appeal lies to the Minister responsible for the corporate registry and must be filed within 30 days of an adverse reconsideration decision; the Minister's determination is subject to judicial review before the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The reserved name is held pending the appeal if the reservation window remains open. Name reservations may thereafter be renewed for successive 30-day validity windows upon payment of the applicable renewal tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Legally permissible: every business corporation must continuously maintain a registered office and a licensed registered agent in the Marshall Islands, but the registered office may be the agent's physical address in Majuro and need not contain the corporation's staff or assets. Nevertheless, given the ISIC 3250 profile — manufacture of turbine-driven critical-care invasive ventilators transacting through government letters of credit and SWIFT wire rails — the FIO, the Ministry of Health, and counterparty banks will expect a locally accessible authorized representative, a documented substance folder showing board decision-making, custody of government contracts, and regulatory contact points, and, where a domestic health permit is pursued, a physical or bonded logistics premise; a pure mail-forwarding arrangement without delegated authority will be treated as impaired substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated at less than 10% for an unannounced registry- or agent-office inspection during the first 12 months for a standard non-resident corporation; however, the likelihood rises to approximately 30% if the entity applies for a domestic Ministry of Health importation or manufacturing permit, or if any PEP or enhanced due diligence flag is recorded, in which case the FIO and the Registrar may conduct a coordinated on-site audit of both the registered agent and any claimed commercial location in Majuro.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and preliminary availability check per candidate corporate name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro (via licensed RMI registered agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Associations Fees Regulations; prevailing market range US$20–US$50 per search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Formal name reservation certificate for the initial 30-day reservation window
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory reservation fee per the Registrar of Corporations' published fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO disclosure preparation, 25%-threshold ownership mapping, identity verification, and source-of-wealth narratives
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed RMI registered agent and FIO-accredited KYC service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of US$350–US$600 per corporate UBO file

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and domestic FIO sanctions screening, including the mandatory 30-day pre-filing re-run
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed RMI registered agent / FIO-accredited screening platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-name and per-jurisdiction screening license fee at market benchmark rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Power of Attorney, certified passport copies, and witness attestations for beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the home jurisdiction of the beneficial owners

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of the Power of Attorney, Good Standing certificates, and certified corporate documents through the RMI Embassies or consular posts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade / designated RMI consular post plus document-forwarding agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular legalization tariff per document, plus agent forwarding fees at market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of bespoke Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, and initial board and officer resolutions tailored to the ISIC 3250 ventilator manufacturing scope
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for non-resident Business Corporation bespoke incorporations under the BCA

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Business Corporations Act filing fee plus certificate issuance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Appointment of the licensed registered agent and establishment of the registered office in Majuro for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual registered-agent and registered-office service retainer; market benchmark US$550–US$900 per year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of the beneficial ownership register and certification of completeness to the Registrar of Corporations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed RMI registered agent on behalf of the Registrar of Corporations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: UBO compliance administration fee at prevailing market benchmark for Beneficial Ownership Act 2021 obligations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ministry of Health statutory license pre-application review for invasive medical device manufacturing and importation under ISIC 3250, including the commercial-substance folder
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Health and Human Services, Majuro, together with RMI-licensed counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory health-licensing application fee plus fixed counsel preparation fee at market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax-exempt status legal opinion and non-resident tax classification memorandum confirming the Tax_Exempt_Zone corporate profile
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for non-resident tax-exempt business corporation opinions

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, 1990 (as amended), Title 24 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code; Sections 8-16 (name reservation, registered agent, registered office, Articles of Incorporation, issuance of Certificate of Incorporation), Sections 39-40 (bylaws and board of directors), and Section 47 (annual franchise tax); foreign ownership is regulated under the Foreign Investment Business License Act 2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro; filings effected through a licensed Registered Agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (RMI Form BC-1) together with the Consent to Act of the Registered Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an RMI Business Corporation. The sole incorporator must subscribe for at least one share (here: one common share, US$0.01 par value) fully paid on issuance; consideration may include cash, promissory notes, or services. No escrow account, paid-up capital certificate, or capital blocking requirement is imposed by the Registrar for the non-resident, tax-exempt structure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscription of the sole Incorporator for One (1) share of Common Stock, US$0.01 par value, be, and hereby is, accepted, and the President is directed to issue Certificate No. 1 to the subscriber. RESOLVED, that the registered office of this Corporation shall be located in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, at the business address of its licensed Registered Agent, which is hereby appointed and approved. RESOLVED, that [Name] is elected Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is elected Secretary, and [Name] is elected Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual meeting. RESOLVED, that the Bylaws submitted to this Board are adopted, and the officers are empowered to open bank accounts and execute all regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands (submitted by a licensed RMI Registered Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name (with 'Corporation', 'Inc.', 'Limited', or an approved abbreviation) via Form BC-0 to the licensed Registered Agent, who lodges the application with the Companies Registry. The Registry checks the name against prohibited or misleading terms and conflicting registrations; an approved name is reserved for 30 days. Simultaneously obtain the notarized Consent to Act from the Registered Agent and fix the Majuro registered-office street address for the Articles.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Application (RMI Form BC-0)
Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Registered Agent
Certified identity documents of the sole incorporator (and certificate of good standing if a corporate incorporator)
Short statement of proposed business purpose (ISIC 3250)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for conflict or prohibited terms, the Registered Agent files a revised application with up to three alternative names within three business days; the original reservation date is retained upon payment of the US$10 rewrite fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole incorporator executes the Articles of Incorporation (Form BC-1) before a notary, declaring the reserved corporate name, the registered office at the Registered Agent's Majuro address, the initial authorized capital (5,000 common shares, par value US$0.01), the non-resident tax-exempt status, and the limited liability clause. The Registered Agent submits the executed Articles, the consent to act, and the government fee to the Companies Registry; the Registry date-stamps the submission and issues an acknowledgement of statutory filing pending the certificate.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation (RMI Form BC-1) in triplicate
Consent to Act as Registered Agent (Form BC-2)
Certificate of Name Reservation
Corporate identification number application data sheet
Payment of the US$350 government filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a notice of deficiency from the Registry, the Registered Agent must cure within five business days by lodging corrective Articles of Amendment; filing priority is preserved and no late penalty attaches if the cure is completed within the statutory cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Charter Posting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the statutory review window, the Registrar certifies the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the unique charter number. The Registered Agent collects the original certificate, arranges an apostille under the Hague Convention where commercial banks in the Government_LC and SWIFT Wire rails require it, and files a notice of incorporation with the Ministry of Finance to obtain the taxpayer reference certificate evidencing the non-resident exempt status.
required_dossiers: Date-stamped Articles of Incorporation
Acknowledgment of statutory filing issued by the Registry
Certificate of Incorporation (original)
Apostille request letter and payment voucher (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond the statutory window, the Registered Agent may file a petition for mandamus in the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands to compel ministerial action; alternatively, a duplicate application may be lodged with an explanatory letter for accelerated certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Bylaws, Share Subscription, and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Business Corporation (internal governance; minuted in the registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole incorporator, acting as first director, signs the corporate Bylaws and convenes the first board meeting or executes a unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting. The board resolves to accept the subscription of one common share, adopt the Registered Agent's Majuro address as the registered office, appoint the Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, and Treasurer, and authorize the opening of bank accounts and all regulatory filings. The resolutions are entered in the statutory minute book and share certificate No. 1 is issued.
required_dossiers: Executed Bylaws of the Corporation
Unanimous Written Consent in lieu of First Board Meeting
Officer and director Declarations of Acceptance
Share register, share certificate stub book, and corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Not applicable — purely internal corporate act; if a conflict with the Bylaws is later identified, the Board adopts a curative resolution subject to ratification at the next annual shareholders' meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) Pre-Operating Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foreign Investment Board, Ministry of Commerce, Investment and Tourism, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because ISIC 3250 life-support ventilator manufacturing is a restricted foreign-investment activity, the newly formed Business Corporation must obtain a Foreign Investment Business License before commencing operations. The Board reviews the ownership structure, background of beneficial owners, and the manufacturing business plan; upon approval it issues an FIBL certificate valid for one year, renewable annually, and the corporation files the certificate with the Companies Registry and tax authorities as a licensing condition.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Business License Application (Form MOA-FIB-01)
Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation
Share register and beneficial-ownership statement
Ventilator-manufacturing business plan (capital, premises, employment, environmental controls)
FIBL application and annual license fee receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A denial may be appealed to the Minister of Commerce within twenty-one days of the decision; a purely documentary deficiency is curable within fourteen days without reopening the substantive review, upon which the application resumes at the stage of the omission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Foreign Investment Board, Ministry of Commerce, Investment and Tourism; Medical Device Regulatory Unit, Ministry of Health and Human Services; Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing Facility Operating Permit (Tier 1) and Foreign Investment Business License (Healthcare Manufacturing)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority, Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report required — Tier II Significant Industrial Facility under the National Environmental Protection Act 1987 and the RMI EPA Operating Permit Regulations 2015; a scoping opinion and an annual environmental compliance certificate are mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Manufacturing process wastewater after treatment must not exceed BOD5 15 mg/L, TSS 20 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0, and residual chlorine 0.5 mg/L prior to discharge; airborne VOC and solvent emissions limited to 2.0 tonnes per year with compliance with WHO 2021 PM2.5/PM10 guideline values; sterilant residues and packaging wastes must be handled through an EPA-licensed hazardous waste contractor, with manifests under the Basel Convention; importation of gas sterilizers must comply with Montreal Protocol ozone-depleting substance prohibitions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety engineering inspection and certification by the Majuro Fire and Rescue Services; structural load and seismic/building code clearance certificate from the Building Inspectorate, Ministry of Public Works; occupational workplace clearance (noise, compressed-gas safety, electrical grounding, and ionizing radiation where applicable) from the Occupational Health and Safety Unit, Ministry of Health and Human Services, issued before machinery commissioning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax and Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Majuro); corporate registration administered by the Office of the Attorney General, Business Corporations Division. Primary filing portal: RMI e-Corporation portal managed by the Registrar of Corporations; no dedicated e-filing portal for tax returns because qualifying non-resident corporations have no tax filing obligation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign owned non-resident Business Corporation (BC) obtains its identity by filing Articles of Incorporation with the Registrar of Corporations through a licensed registered agent under the Business Corporations Act 1990 (as amended). No separate TIN application is required: the certificate of incorporation and the statutory declaration that the corporation will not carry on business in the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) constitute the tax identity instrument. For customs/import purposes, a separate Customs Registration Number is obtainable from the Tax and Customs Administration upon first import; where a physical presence is intended, an import license/permit is required under the RMI Business License Act. Foreign entities have no obligation to obtain an RMI tax identification number unless they establish a taxable nexus.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: RMI law does not adopt US check-the-box classification; entity tax status is fixed by statute. The operative 'election' is the non-resident domestic corporation status under Section 42 of the Business Corporations Act: a BC is automatically and irrevocably exempt from all RMI income, capital gains, withholding, and franchise taxes provided it (i) maintains a registered agent and office in RMI, (ii) files an annual listing fee and statement, and (iii) does not carry on any business or hold a commercial license in RMI. No hybrid mismatch or entity reclassification elections exist in RMI domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Import Duty / Customs Tariff (no VAT, GST, or Sales and Use Tax in force in the Republic of the Marshall Islands; indirect taxation is levied exclusively at the point of customs importation, supplemented by specific excises on alcohol, tobacco, and fuel)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis turnover threshold: all importers of commercial goods must register with the Tax and Customs Administration and obtain an Importer Code / Customs Registration; the general ad valorem import duty rate is 8%, with reduced rates (0% for medical/life-saving items, books, basic foods) and higher rates up to 100%+ for luxury goods under the RMI Import Duty Schedule.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API data exchange, or digital stamping regime exists for domestic sales or exports. Customs clearance is effected via standardized customs declaration forms and shipping manifests; a limited electronic customs declaration interface is available at the Majuro Customs Office for commercial filers, but real-time government fiscal clearance of commercial e-invoices is not mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable under an import-duty-only system: RMI imposes no VAT/GST on domestic or export supply, and no export duty is levied on goods manufactured in or exported from RMI. Accordingly, the export of ICU mechanical ventilators and turbine-driven critical care components obtains an absolute exemption from indirect taxation by virtue of the absence of any export VAT/GST charge; no refund claim mechanism is required. The only fiscal condition is that the goods are physically exported and presented to RMI Customs with an outbound manifest to preclude any allegation of import-duty evasion if goods re-enter the domestic market.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial Invoice (in English, showing exporter, consignee, incoterms, HS codes 9019.20 / 8414.80 if turbine components separate)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Packing List with gross/net weights and container/seal numbers
Certificate of Origin (optional, for preferential tariff access in destination markets)
Import License from destination country (for regulated medical devices, where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT zero-rating refund or clawback regime exists because no VAT is chargeable. The relevant compliance risk is the loss of statutory tax exemption: if a BC conducts business in RMI (e.g., local warehousing, physical sales, or maintaining a commercial office) without a business license, the exemption under Section 42 of the Business Corporations Act is voidable retroactively, exposing the entity to annual license fees, additional government service charges, and penalties under the Business License Act 1991 (up to USD 1,000 per month of unlicensed activity). Customs fraud or false export declarations attract penalties under the RMI Customs Act, including forfeiture of goods, fines up to three times the value of the goods, and imprisonment for deliberate false declarations. The RMI Trade Remedies and Subsidies (Commerce Act) may also impose countervailing duties if export incentives are found to distort trade, but standard RMI exports of lawful manufactured medical goods carry no such exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) maintains no conventional central bank or monetary authority; the Banking Commission, established under the Banking Act 1993 (as amended by the Banking (Amendment) Acts 1996 and 2000), headquartered in Majuro and headed by the Banking Commissioner, is the sole prudential regulator and licensing body for all deposit-taking institutions, while the United States dollar (USD) is the sole legal tender and the US Federal Reserve System operates as the de facto currency-issuing, clearing, and settlement backstop.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: De jure fully convertible: the RMI is a completely dollarized economy with no foreign-exchange-control law, no capital-account restrictions, and no statutory distinction between current-account and capital-account convertibility. Non-resident Business Corporations organized under the Business Corporations Act (modeled on Delaware law and administered by the RMI Corporate Registrar) are income-tax-exempt, and the RMI imposes no withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or profit-remittance flows to foreign shareholders, so profit repatriation is legally unobstructed. De facto frictions arise exclusively from correspondent-bank de-risking pressure, concentration of USD liquidity in the two licensed banks (Bank of Marshall Islands and Bank of Guam, Majuro branch), and the KYC requirement to evidence real economic substance; none of these impose quantitative conversion limits, but they create documentation lead time and enhanced-due-diligence cost.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None apply. The RMI imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export receipts. A non-resident BC may retain ICU-ventilator export revenues in USD or in any freely convertible foreign currency within a licensed bank, may deploy them directly against inbound component-supplier payments, or may earmark them as letter-of-credit collateral. The only binding obligations arise from the RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2013 (as amended): full transaction record-keeping, beneficial-ownership disclosure for every natural person holding 10% or more of the BC, and the licensed bank's independent duty to file suspicious-transaction reports on material trade flows.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD current account; optional capital-escrow module with no statutory minimum paid-in capital required for an RMI BC, although BMI internally requires a reasonable opening balance and maintenance of cleared USD funds

USD operational account with full US Fedwire and automated-clearing integrated settlement, commercial letter-of-credit desk (MT700 series), and pre-export liquidity sweep facility; standby capital-escrow account for paid-in share capital

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW - legally not viable onshore. The RMI Banking Act requires a Banking Commission license for any deposit-taking activity and contains no charter, licensing, or supervisory category for electronic-money institutions, payment institutions, or specialized cross-border wallet providers; the 2018 Sovereign (SOV) digital-currency statute is a monetary-policy experiment that creates no payment-service licensing utility. Offshore fintech EMIs may service a non-resident BC only as an unregulated payment channel and face pervasive correspondent de-risking when routing through the RMI's US-bank clearing rails; an offshore EMI is acceptable only in a limited treasury role (for example, a top-tier EEA-licensed EMI used strictly for supplier payouts outside the RMI) and may never be positioned as the sole liquidity or settlement bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory when opening at either licensed bank: at least one director, the company secretary, or an expressly authorized signatory holding the BC's registered-agent power of attorney must attend an in-person KYC and beneficial-ownership interview at the Majuro branch. Purely remote opening is not published as a standard product and is granted only on an enhanced-due-diligence committee waiver after (i) the RMI registered agent certifies the Articles of Incorporation, bylaws, and certificate of incumbency, (ii) a bank-to-bank reference is delivered from the shareholder's home-country bank, (iii) notarized and apostilled or consular-legalized copies of all signatory identity and corporate documents are lodged, and (iv) the committee approves, typically within 6-10 weeks. For a non-resident BC with 100% foreign ownership, the UBO declaration covering every natural person with 10% or greater interest is strictly non-waivable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt non-resident BC without visible economic substance: registered-agent custody patterns, nominee-shareholder indicators, zero local payroll, and no premises raise a shell-company red flag at onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidentiary defense bundle: (1) current certificate of good standing and complete registered-agent corporate records from the RMI-licensed agent; (2) certified Articles of Incorporation and bylaws; (3) audited opening financial statements or an accountant-certified opening-balance ledger; (4) completed UBO register and source-of-wealth narrative signed by each 10%+ shareholder; (5) physical-substance file comprising the ventilator-factory lease, equipment invoices, production photographs, and payroll records of the manufacturing workforce; (6) statutory plant license and ISO 13485 quality-management certificate; (7) a five-year business plan and customer pipeline confirming an arm's-length commercial purpose for the non-resident structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Government letter-of-credit and public-procurement funds as the primary revenue channel: state-purchaser flows, potential end-user ambiguity, and sanctions or export-control exposure for ICU ventilators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidentiary defense bundle: (1) fully executed government purchase order and tender-award documentation; (2) signed end-user certificate and no-re-export undertaking; (3) archived sanctions-screening outputs (UN, OFAC, EU consolidated lists) showing clear results for all counterparties, banks, and ports; (4) export license, customs declarations, and freight-forwarder confirmations for each outbound shipment; (5) medical-device quality compliance file (ISO 13485 registration and target-market regulatory authorization of the ventilator); (6) correspondent-bank references and, where obtainable, a confirming bank's pre-acceptance of future government LCs to neutralize sovereign-payment and bank-risk objections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medium-Risk-Enhanced rating for the life-support hardware manufacturing sector: high-value trade flows, component suppliers across multiple jurisdictions, and urgent government procurement timelines increase monitoring intensity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidentiary defense bundle: (1) FDA-equivalent or target-market regulatory approval of the ICU ventilator; (2) distribution, OEM, and supplier agreements mapped by jurisdiction with invoices, bills of lading, and incoterms for every trade transaction; (3) a 12-month treasury cash-flow forecast matching capital injections to capital calls; (4) appointment of a designated AML/compliance officer and board-adopted internal AML, sanctions-screening, and KYC policy; (5) a written undertaking to provide quarterly transaction-level reporting to the account bank while the Enhanced rating persists; (6) updated UBO and physical-substance documentation filed within 30 days of any ownership or management change.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound equity: (i) execute SWIFT MT103 transfers in USD to the BC's USD account at Bank of Guam Majuro or Bank of Marshall Islands with the ordering-customer field showing the true remitter and the beneficiary field matching the exact registered corporate name; (ii) use payment references stating 'Paid-in share capital contribution' and, where the US correspondent requires a purpose code, the standard investment or equity-transfer classification (for example, TRFI, transfer of funds for investment, or its equivalent); (iii) pre-load UBO declarations and source-of-funds letters before the first credit so the receiving bank releases funds without hold; (iv) if any business is conducted inside the RMI, obtain a Foreign Investment Business License under the Foreign Investment Business Act 1997 before injecting capital, while noting that a purely non-resident manufacturer-exporter does not require a FIBL; (v) ensure all messages carry the full legal identity of both sender and beneficiary to satisfy FATF Recommendation 16 travel-rule data expectations of the US correspondent clearing network.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound trade: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct wires for supplier, freight, and component payments as the dominant rail for speed and traceability; (ii) commercial letters of credit for import and export settlements issued through Bank of Guam's MT700 series, amended by MT707, and advised or paid via MT710/MT754, with standby reimbursement by MT760; (iii) documentary collections for smaller tranches of the government-LC flow; (iv) the domestic clearing backbone is the US Fedwire and automated-clearing correspondent network, giving same-day USD settlement because RMI banks maintain US correspondent accounts rather than operating an island-based clearing house; (v) for the ICU-ventilator government procurement channel, the optimal structure is a confirmed irrevocable export letter of credit with a top-tier US or European confirming bank, converting sovereign and issuing-bank risk into the confirming bank's obligation while the local RMI bank handles documentary presentation only.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts executed offshore with the Bank of Guam dealing room or a top-tier international dealer to fix EUR/USD, GBP/USD, CNY/USD, and JPY/USD conversion of export prices on committed government purchase orders

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) booked under the ISDA 1998 FX Definitions for currencies without an onshore deliverable RMI market, used when the purchasing government's currency is restricted or soft

Cross-currency swaps (MT300 confirmation) matching long-dated government-LC receipts against foreign-currency supplier liabilities, executed under a bilateral ISDA agreement outside RMI prudential reach

FX options and zero-cost collars purchased from an offshore executing broker, permissible because RMI banking law regulates deposit-taking institutions and does not restrict a non-resident BC's use of offshore derivatives

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report (Form 6) under Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation (calendar-anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: US$ 250 late fee after 30 days; 60 days arrears triggers administrative suspension; continued non-filing for 3 months results in certificate of non-compliance and strike-off from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register and Share Transfer Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent resident in Marshall Islands (acting for Registrar and Financial Intelligence Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the Annual Corporate Report; must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML/CFT licensing sanction against registered agent; corporate entity may incur US$ 500 administrative fine and mandatory filing of annual UBO declaration in the following year.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory annual statutory audit for a non-resident Business Corporation under the Business Corporations Act, except when requested by shareholders holding at least 10% of issued voting shares, or when annual gross turnover exceeds US$ 2,000,000, or when the corporation is listed or regulated as a public financing entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by IASB; local Marshall Islands GAAP may be used only for internal management accounts of non-resident business corporations that are not subject to a public audit requirement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every registered business corporation must file with its registered agent an annual UBO confirmation listing all beneficial owners as at the anniversary date. A share transfer triggers an additional confirmation within 15 days of registration of the transfer. The registered agent must record transfers in the register of members and submit the UBO confirmation to the Registrar only if a beneficial ownership change is deemed notifiable under the Marshall Islands AML/CFT regulations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (NRDC) under section 6 of the Nonresident Business Corporations Act 1998; reference resident corporate rate is 3% gross receipts tax on RMI-source gross income under section 8(a)(1) of the Income Tax Act 1989
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Infinite-horizon (50-year) statutory tax exemption covering income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duties; the registered NRDC is a tax-exempt-zone entity and pays only the annual government fee (US$500 for authorized capital up to US$50,000, graduated thereafter) and registered-agent fees; the foreign operating manufacturing entity is not subject to any RMI corporate tax on foreign-source revenue

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No RMI corporate income tax return is prescribed for an NRDC. The sole annual statutory filing is the Annual Report (Form BCA-AR / NRDC Annual Report) submitted to the Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations through the Registrar's online filing portal (Registrar Web / RW System) by a licensed RMI registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one filing per calendar year; no quarterly corporate tax installments or provisional returns are imposed on an exempt NRDC)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Report and the concurrent annual government fee are due on or before April 30 of each calendar year; the Registrar's renewal invoice cycle is aligned to the month of incorporation anniversary. No tax-return deadline exists because the NRDC has zero assessed tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal name and registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact name and BC number shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; any inconsistency blocks renewal of the 50-year tax exemption certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent and registered office address in Majuro
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the licensed RMI registered agent and Majuro address; the NRDC need not maintain a physical staffed office in the Marshall Islands.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business address and jurisdiction of manufacturing operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the true foreign operating address of the ventilator manufacturing facility (e.g., parent-plant location) and certify that no business is conducted inside the RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident status declaration and Tax Exemption Certificate number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Affirm NRDC status under the Nonresident Business Corporations Act 1998 and reference the exemption certificate number; declaring any RMI-source income would jeopardize the exemption.
State authorized capital in USD; annual government fee is computed on authorized capital; overstatement increases the fee and understatement may trigger Registrar rejection.
List each ultimate beneficial owner, nationality, and tax residence; a false beneficial-ownership statement invalidates the exemption certificate and constitutes a criminal offense.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file triggers: (i) a late-filing penalty of US$100 per commenced month of arrears; (ii) administrative dissolution or strike-off after approximately 90 days of arrears; (iii) a reinstatement fee of US$300 plus all unpaid annual fees; (iv) no daily income-tax surcharge applies because no income tax return is filed for NRDCs; willful or false filing additionally exposes officers to fines up to US$50,000 under Business Corporations Act penalty provisions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — the RMI imposes no dividend withholding tax on distributions made by an NRDC, and section 6 of the Nonresident Business Corporations Act 1998 bars the introduction of any new withholding tax against the exempt corporation during the 50-year exemption period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has no double taxation agreement (DTA) network granting reduced withholding rates; it maintains only tax information exchange agreements (TIEAs), which do not provide rate relief. To invoke exemption abroad, the NRDC must: (i) request a Tax Exemption Certificate / Tax Residence Certificate from the RMI Registrar (issued within 5 to 10 business days upon payment of the annual government fee, no tax clearance needed); (ii) deliver the certificate with the Certificate of Incorporation and a non-resident status declaration to the foreign paying counterparty; (iii) satisfy the foreign jurisdiction's domestic beneficial-ownership and substance conditions. The RMI certificate does not override CFC, General Anti-Avoidance Rule, or substance-based denial rules in the shareholder's state.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Non-exempt statutory withholding is 15% under section 15 of the Income Tax Act 1989 for RMI-source interest, royalties, rents, and dividends paid to non-residents; however, royalties and interest paid outbound by an NRDC to foreign IP owners and lenders are subject to 0% RMI withholding because the NRDC is tax-exempt and has no RMI-source income; no treaty-reduced rates are available in the RMI tax treaty network.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable — the RMI has not enacted transfer-pricing, Local File, Master File, or country-by-country reporting rules. The relevant international threshold is the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework GloBE (Pillar Two) consolidation test of EUR 750 million in group revenue, which the RMI, as an Inclusive Framework member, is expected to implement for RMI constituent entities; functional currency for any records is USD.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI does not administer EU-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); section 6 of the Nonresident Business Corporations Act 1998 requires only a registered agent, a registered office in Majuro, a non-resident declaration, and a certification of no business with RMI residents. The EU Code of Practice Group continues to screen the RMI for 'no or only nominal taxation' status (recurring Annex I / Annex II listing), so commercial substance (actual manufacturing capability, qualified personnel, binding supply contracts, operational bank accounts in the manufacturing jurisdiction) is essential to protect the transaction and to avoid beneficial-ownership denial or treaty-shopping findings in the destination market.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Abuse of the NRDC Tax Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deriving RMI-source income or conducting business with RMI residents while claiming the section 6 exemption; making false non-resident declarations; using the exempt BC as an artificial conduit to strip profits from a taxable manufacturing operation without operational substance or arm's-length remuneration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive revocation of the Tax Exemption Certificate; assessment of the 3% gross receipts tax on all RMI-source receipts plus delinquency penalties up to 100% and statutory interest; criminal fines up to US$50,000 under the Business Corporations Act; possible debarment from Marshall Islands government procurement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations commit perjury and may face imprisonment for up to 10 years; courts may pierce the corporate veil to impose joint and several liability for the evaded tax, penalties, and interest; civil restitution orders, travel bans, and asset freezes may be issued by the High Court of the RMI.
